quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: At night, how should you look to reduce headlight glare?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are bright, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, pull off the road and let other vehicles pass. Only drive below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: An upcoming curve in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive in the right lane only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without emergency braking. This protects the driver behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use your brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: During a tire blowout, release the gas pedal first. Do not brake right away. Then gradually slow down and gently apply the brakes while pulling off the road.

questions.question: What traffic light will soon appear after a steady yellow light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will come next.

questions.question: What should a small vehicle driver be ready for when passing a large vehicle?

options.text: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Small vehicle drivers should be ready to steer correctly when passing or meeting large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped as long as the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must make hand signals to communicate.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, what must a driver do?

options.text: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Wait for a safe time to merge into traffic.

questions.question: What do some highways use to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows on the road show which lanes to use for driving straight or turning.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. What should your headlights be on?

options.text: Either high or low beam setting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is approaching or when you are following another vehicle. Use the low beam setting to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to quickly pass the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must slow down and change lanes if you can do so safely. If changing lanes is not possible, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, what should drivers do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk and pass the bus on its left.
Continue driving when you think children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus shows its stop signal, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign tell you?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange signs show construction, maintenance, and emergency work areas.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before the intersection.

questions.question: How must a driver treat pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the circumstances. Always watch for pedestrians and yield the right-of-way to all of them, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Your tires work less well when you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Roads become more slippery when you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires work less well when you drive faster.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water from the road as well. If you go too fast, your tires will lose grip and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Orange signs mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones on highways. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians you might hit. For example, if another driver does not see you and is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot drive in this direction.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Also watch for other warning signs like a lowered gate or the sound of a train.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from your seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare you for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions less than perfect. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will hit the curb and stop.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze faster than sunny areas. They also take longer to thaw. Be extra careful on roads in shadow from trees or buildings.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed limit in a business district is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a business district is 30 mph unless a different speed is posted.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking their rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Slow down gradually and check your mirrors. Move to the left lane before the intersection. Watch for other cars and pedestrians. Only turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.
Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles. Pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on wet roads. You can reduce this risk by driving slower on wet roads, keeping tires at the right air pressure, and replacing worn tires.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers to yield.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs mean yield. Slow down and be ready to stop. Go only when the road is clear.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low railroad crossing. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or catch on the tracks.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles like trucks and SUVs have bigger blind spots. Areas near the back cannot be seen in their side or rearview mirrors.
